name: Cetus
introduction: is the sea monster sent to devour Andromeda. It is the fourth-largest constellation, sprawling across a sky region known as “the Sea”, with few bright stars. It straddles the celestial equator and is best seen on autumn evenings.

sections.title: What makes it special
paragraphs: Cetus contains [Mira](hip:10826), “the Wonderful”, the first star known to vary regularly in brightness. Over about 11 months, this pulsating red giant rises to naked-eye brightness and then fades from view, becoming hundreds of times fainter. In 2007, ultraviolet images revealed that Mira trails a 13-light-year tail of material as it races through space.

[Tau Ceti](hip:8102), only 12 light-years away, is one of the nearest single stars similar to the Sun. In 1960, it was one of the first two targets of Project Ozma, the first radio search for extraterrestrial intelligence.

sections.title: Notable stars
paragraphs: [Diphda](hip:3419), the brightest star, is an orange giant 96 light-years away, and [Menkar](hip:14135) is a red giant marking the monster’s jaw.

Cetus has several nearby red dwarfs. [UV Ceti](id:luyten-726-8-a), about 9 light-years away, is the prototype of flare stars, which can brighten many times in minutes. [YZ Ceti](id:10pc-0049) has three small, rocky planets.

sections.title: Beyond the stars
paragraphs: M77 is a bright spiral galaxy with an active nucleus, one of the first Seyfert galaxies identified. The dwarf galaxies IC 1613 and Wolf–Lundmark–Melotte are members of our Local Group.
